evidence: src/domain/product.ts: Product.reserve checks `if (quantity > this.available)` and throws DomainError("INSUFFICIENT_STOCK", `Insufficient stock for product ${this.id}: requested ${quantity}, available ${this.available}`)

src/domain/stock-allocation-service.ts: StockAllocationService.reserve checks `if (line.quantity > product.availableQuantity)` and throws DomainError("INSUFFICIENT_STOCK", `Insufficient stock for product ${product.id}: requested ${line.quantity}, available ${product.availableQuantity}`)
src/domain/order.ts and src/domain/order-status.ts: transition rules are consistently kept in order-status (nextFulfilmentStatus, isCancellable) and only used by Order: no duplication there
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module covers one domain concern: ordering and stock reservation. `Order`, `OrderLine` and `order-status` keep the lifecycle rules in one place (`nextFulfilmentStatus`, `isCancellable`, `FULFILMENT_FLOW`). The repository interfaces are clean ports, and all errors go through `DomainError`. The problem is that the stock-sufficiency rule exists twice. `Product.reserve` enforces `quantity > available` and throws INSUFFICIENT_STOCK. `StockAllocationService.reserve` copies that comparison and the error message using `product.availableQuantity`, instead of asking `Product` through a method of its own. The pre-check makes multi-line reservations all-or-nothing, which is a reasonable goal. Even so, the rule now has to be maintained in two files, which the rubric counts as a failure.

violations.message: StockAllocationService.reserve copies Product's stock rule (`line.quantity > product.availableQuantity`, with the same INSUFFICIENT_STOCK message) instead of asking Product. The rule now lives in both product.ts and this file. Fix: add a check method to Product, such as canReserve or assertCanReserve, and call it for the all-or-nothing pre-check.
